top_choice_rationale: Halide perovskites are a new semiconductor family whose behaviour is explained by a checkable structural chemistry (corner-sharing ABX3 lattice, soft defect-tolerant framework, tunable gap), replicated worldwide for over a decade, and the Miyasaka, Park, Snaith chain of 2009, 2012 and 2012-13 steps is short and independently confirmed by several members. Stability and lead toxicity argue for caution but do not negate the demonstrated discovery; ionizable lipid nanoparticles (P001) are the strongest alternative on maturity but have unresolved credit among Vancouver, MIT and Acuitas lines.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Stockholm University colleague of Peter Brzezinski, and professional familiarity with the porous-materials community, neither bearing on the proposals in the slate
